issues.where: (the seat of Kapha) ... (the seat of Vāta)
issues.problem: The parenthetical doctrine of the seats of Kapha and Vāta is imported from outside the verse; the order-based reading needs only the verse.
issues.fix: Probably to be read in order: drying first for Vāta in the āmāśaya, oleation first for Kapha in the pakvāśaya; the verse states the two kinds in the same order as the two conditions.

patch.value: Probably to be read in order: drying first for Vāta in the āmāśaya, oleation first for Kapha in the pakvāśaya; the verse states the two kinds in the same order as the two conditions.

issues.problem: śeṣa is an adjective usable in the masculine; śeṣam here is m. acc. sg. agreeing with aṅgāvayavam ('the remaining parts of the body'). The n. label and the note about a gender mismatch are wrong.

patch.value: śeṣam (m. acc. sg.) agrees with aṅgāvayavam: 'the remaining parts of the body'.

issues.problem: Tasyāśitīya is a derivative in -īya from the phrase tasya aśita, not a compound; 'aśitīye' is not a word by itself. The note's 'it is named in this verse' is redundant.
issues.fix: w 'tasyāśitīye', gram 'm. loc. sg. (chapter name, derivative in -īya)'; note reworded

patch.value: m. loc. sg. (chapter name, derivative in -īya)
Tasyāśitīya is the name of a chapter, a derivative in -īya from the words tasya aśita; it is not split into compound members.

issues.problem: Flag upheld (āḍya is not a Sanskrit word; āḍhya is). The 'why' should cite the checkable evidence instead of a vague 'elsewhere': the same edition prints आढ्यवात at 06.28.66a (text/ch06.28.md).

patch.value: āḍya is not a Sanskrit word; āḍhya 'rich' gives āḍhyaroga. The same edition prints āḍhya in āḍhyavāta at 06.28.66a (text/ch06.28.md). Probable typo of ḍ for ḍh.

issues.problem: Draft is right not to correct: in this even pāda the 6th syllable must be long (ka-rī-ṣā-ya-sa-PŪ-ṭa-kaiḥ), so puṭaka would break the metre. But pūṭaka is not a known word in this form, so the gloss 'packets' is conjectural and should say so.

patch.text: pūṭaka is not a known word in this form; the meaning 'packet' rests on reading it as puṭaka and is conjectural.
